passages.text: What I am saying is that as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, although he is the owner of everything.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians in Galatia.
Paul explains the status of an heir.
An heir is a person who will inherit everything from his father.
If the heir is still a child, he has no real difference from a slave.
The child is the future owner of everything.
But while he is a child, he does not have control.
He is not free to act as the master.
passages.original: Λέγω δέ ἐφ’ ὅσον χρόνον ὁ κληρονόμος νήπιός ἐστιν οὐδὲν διαφέρει δούλου κύριος πάντων ὤν

passages.text: He is subject to guardians and trustees until the date set by his father.
passages.sermon:
The heir is a child.
He is not free to manage everything.
He must obey guardians.
He must obey trustees.
He stays under their authority.
This lasts until the father sets a time.
The father decides when the child receives full rights.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ ἐπιτρόπους ἐστὶν καὶ οἰκονόμους ἄχρι τῆς προθεσμίας τοῦ πατρός

passages.text: So also, when we were children, we were enslaved under the basic principles of the world.
passages.sermon:
We were once children.
We did not have maturity.
We lived under the basic principles of the world.
These principles controlled us.
We were enslaved by them.
passages.original: οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς ὅτε ἦμεν νήπιοι ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου ἤμεθα δεδουλωμένοι

passages.text: But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law, to redeem those under the law, that we might receive our adoption as sons.
passages.sermon:
God acted when the right time arrived.
God sent His Son.
God’s Son was born from a woman.
God’s Son was born under the law.
God sent His Son to redeem people under the law.
God did this so we could receive adoption as sons.
passages.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ χρόνου ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸν Υἱὸν αὐτοῦ γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός γενόμενον ὑπὸ νόμον ἵνα τοὺς ὑπὸ νόμον ἐξαγοράσῃ ἵνα τὴν υἱοθεσίαν ἀπολάβωμεν

passages.text: And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, “Abba, Father!”
passages.sermon:
You are sons of God.
God sent the Spirit of His Son.
God sent this Spirit into our hearts.
The Spirit cries out in our hearts.
The Spirit says, “Abba, Father!”
passages.original: Ὅτι δέ ἐστε υἱοί ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς καρδίας ἡμῶν κρᾶζον Ἀββᾶ ὁ Πατήρ

passages.text: So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and since you are a son, you are also an heir through God.
passages.sermon:
You are not a slave now.
You are a son now.
God made you a son.
Because you are a son, you are also an heir.
God made you an heir.
passages.original: ὥστε οὐκέτι εἶ δοῦλος ἀλλὰ υἱός εἰ δὲ υἱός καὶ κληρονόμος διὰ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Formerly, when you did not know God, you were slaves to those who by nature are not gods.
passages.sermon: You did not know God before.\r\nYou served things that are not gods by nature.\r\nYou were slaves to these things.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ τότε μὲν οὐκ εἰδότες Θεὸν ἐδουλεύσατε τοῖς φύσει μὴ οὖσιν θεοῖς

passages.text: But now that you know God, or rather are known by God, how is it that you are turning back to those weak and worthless principles? Do you wish to be enslaved by them all over again?
passages.sermon:
You now know God.
God also knows you.
You once did not know God.
You served things that are not truly gods.
Now you know the true God.
God has made Himself known to you.
Why do you turn back to weak principles?
These principles have no real value.
You want to serve them again.
You want to be slaves to them again.
passages.original: νῦν δὲ γνόντες Θεόν μᾶλλον δὲ γνωσθέντες ὑπὸ Θεοῦ πῶς ἐπιστρέφετε πάλιν ἐπὶ τὰ ἀσθενῆ καὶ πτωχὰ στοιχεῖα οἷς πάλιν ἄνωθεν δουλεύειν θέλετε

passages.text: You are observing special days and months and seasons and years!
passages.sermon:
You observe special days.
You observe special months.
You observe special seasons.
You observe special years.
passages.original: ἡμέρας παρατηρεῖσθε καὶ μῆνας καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἐνιαυτούς

passages.text: I fear for you, that my efforts for you may have been in vain.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the believers in Galatia.
Paul feels concern for them.
Paul fears that his work among them may have no lasting result.
Paul worries that his efforts for them might be wasted.
Paul expresses this fear directly to them.
passages.original: φοβοῦμαι ὑμᾶς μή πως εἰκῇ κεκοπίακα εἰς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: I beg you, brothers, become like me, for I became like you. You have done me no wrong.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Galatians as brothers.
Paul begs the Galatians to become like him.
Paul became like the Galatians.
The Galatians have done Paul no wrong.
passages.original: Γίνεσθε ὡς ἐγώ ὅτι κἀγὼ ὡς ὑμεῖς ἀδελφοί δέομαι ὑμῶν οὐδέν με ἠδικήσατε

passages.text: You know that it was because of an illness that I first preached the gospel to you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the one speaking.
Paul first preached the gospel to you.
Paul preached to you because he was ill.
You know this.
passages.original: Οἴδατε δὲ ὅτι δι’ ἀσθένειαν τῆς σαρκὸς εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν τὸ πρότερον

passages.text: And although my illness was a trial to you, you did not despise or reject me. Instead, you welcomed me as if I were an angel of God, as if I were Christ Jesus Himself.
passages.sermon:
Paul was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul had an illness in his body.
Paul’s illness was a trial for the Galatians.
The Galatians did not despise Paul because of his illness.
The Galatians did not reject Paul because of his illness.
The Galatians welcomed Paul.
They received Paul as if he were an angel from God.
They received Paul as if he were Christ Jesus Himself.
passages.original: καὶ τὸν πειρασμὸν ὑμῶν ἐν τῇ σαρκί μου οὐκ ἐξουθενήσατε οὐδὲ ἐξεπτύσατε ἀλλὰ ὡς ἄγγελον Θεοῦ ἐδέξασθέ με ὡς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: What then has become of your blessing? For I can testify that, if it were possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Galatians.
\r\nPaul reminds them of their past kindness.
\r\nPaul asks, “What has happened to your blessing?”
\r\nPaul testifies about their love.
\r\nPaul says, “If you could have, you would have given me your eyes.”
\r\nPaul means they cared for him deeply.
\r\nPaul remembers their willingness to sacrifice for him.
passages.original: ποῦ οὖν ὁ μακαρισμὸς ὑμῶν μαρτυρῶ γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰ δυνατὸν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὑμῶν ἐξορύξαντες ἐδώκατέ μοι

passages.text: Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?
passages.sermon:
I speak the truth to you.
I tell you what is right.
I do not lie to you.
I want you to know the truth.
Now, do you see me as your enemy?
Have I become your enemy because I tell you the truth?
passages.original: ὥστε ἐχθρὸς ὑμῶν γέγονα ἀληθεύων ὑμῖν

passages.text: Those people are zealous for you, but not in a good way. Instead, they want to isolate you from us, so that you may be zealous for them.
passages.sermon:
Some people show zeal for you.
They do not do this in a good way.
They want to separate you from us.
They want you to be zealous for them.
passages.original: Ζηλοῦσιν ὑμᾶς οὐ καλῶς ἀλλὰ ἐκκλεῖσαι ὑμᾶς θέλουσιν ἵνα αὐτοὺς ζηλοῦτε

passages.text: Nevertheless, it is good to be zealous if it serves a noble purpose—at any time, and not only when I am with you.
passages.sermon:
Zeal can be good.
Zeal is good when it serves a noble purpose.
It is good to be zealous at any time.
It is good to be zealous not only when I am with you.
passages.original: καλὸν δὲ ζηλοῦσθαι ἐν καλῷ πάντοτε καὶ μὴ μόνον ἐν τῷ παρεῖναί με πρὸς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: My children, for whom I am again in the pains of childbirth until Christ is formed in you, how I wish I could be with you now and change my tone, because I am perplexed about you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Galatians.
Paul calls the Galatians his children.
Paul feels deep concern for them.
Paul says he is suffering again for them.
Paul compares his suffering to the pains of childbirth.
Paul wants Christ to be formed in them.
Paul wishes he could be with them now.
Paul wants to change his tone when he speaks to them.
Paul feels perplexed about them.
passages.original: Τέκνα μου οὓς πάλιν ὠδίνω μέχρις οὗ μορφωθῇ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν ἤθελον δὲ παρεῖναι πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἄρτι καὶ ἀλλάξαι τὴν φωνήν μου ὅτι ἀποροῦμαι ἐν ὑμῖν

passages.text: Tell me, you who want to be under the law, do you not understand what the law says?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Galatians.
Some people want to live under the law.
Paul asks them a question.
He says, “Tell me, you who want to be under the law.”
He asks, “Do you not understand what the law says?”
passages.original: Λέγετέ μοι οἱ ὑπὸ νόμον θέλοντες εἶναι τὸν νόμον οὐκ ἀκούετε

passages.text: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and the other by the free woman.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man chosen by God.
Abraham had two sons.
One son was born from a slave woman.
One son was born from a free woman.
Scripture records this.
passages.original: γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Ἀβραὰμ δύο υἱοὺς ἔσχεν ἕνα ἐκ τῆς παιδίσκης καὶ ἕνα ἐκ τῆς ἐλευθέρας

passages.text: His son by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, but his son by the free woman was born through the promise.
passages.sermon:
Abraham had two sons.
One son was born to the slave woman Hagar.
This son was born in a natural, human way.
The other son was born to the free woman Sarah.
This son was born because God made a promise.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ὁ μὲν ἐκ τῆς παιδίσκης κατὰ σάρκα γεγέννηται ὁ δὲ ἐκ τῆς ἐλευθέρας δι’ τῆς ἐπαγγελίας

passages.text: These things serve as illustrations, for the women represent two covenants. One covenant is from Mount Sinai and bears children into slavery: This is Hagar.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes about Abraham’s two sons.
He says these things are illustrations.
The two women represent two covenants.
One covenant comes from Mount Sinai.
This covenant gives birth to slavery.
Hagar is this covenant.
passages.original: ἅτινά ἐστιν ἀλληγορούμενα αὗται γάρ εἰσιν δύο διαθῆκαι μία μὲν ἀπὸ ὄρους Σινᾶ εἰς δουλείαν γεννῶσα ἥτις ἐστὶν Ἁγάρ

passages.text: Now Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem, because she is in slavery with her children.
passages.sermon:
Hagar represents Mount Sinai.
Mount Sinai is in Arabia.
Hagar also corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem.
Hagar is in slavery with her children.
Present-day Jerusalem is also in slavery with her children.
passages.original: τὸ δὲ Ἁγὰρ Σινᾶ ὄρος ἐστὶν ἐν τῇ Ἀραβίᾳ συστοιχεῖ δὲ τῇ νῦν Ἰερουσαλήμ δουλεύει γὰρ μετὰ τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς

passages.text: But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.
passages.sermon:
The Jerusalem above is free.
This Jerusalem is not on earth.
This Jerusalem is from heaven.
This Jerusalem is our mother.
She gives us freedom.
passages.original: ἡ δὲ ἄνω Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐλευθέρα ἐστίν ἥτις ἐστὶν μήτηρ ἡμῶν

passages.text: For it is written: “Rejoice, O barren woman, who bears no children; break forth and cry aloud, you who have never travailed; because more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband.”
passages.sermon:
The Scripture says this.
It says, “Rejoice, barren woman.”
The barren woman does not give birth to children.
It says, “Break forth and cry aloud, you who have never felt labor pains.”
The woman who has no children is desolate.
The desolate woman will have many children.
She will have more children than the woman who has a husband.
passages.original: γέγραπται γάρ Εὐφράνθητι στεῖρα ἡ οὐ τίκτουσα ῥῆξον καὶ βόησον ἡ οὐκ ὠδίνουσα ὅτι πολλὰ τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐρήμου μᾶλλον ἢ τῆς ἐχούσης τὸν ἄνδρα

passages.text: Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Galatia.
He calls them brothers.
He says they are like Isaac.
Isaac was Abraham’s son.
God promised Isaac would be born.
Paul says the believers are children of promise.
God gave them this promise.
They belong to God’s family because of His promise.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἀδελφοί κατὰ Ἰσαὰκ ἐπαγγελίας τέκνα ἐστέ

passages.text: At that time, however, the son born by the flesh persecuted the son born by the Spirit. It is the same now.
passages.sermon:
At that time, there were two sons.
One son was born by the flesh.
The other son was born by the Spirit.
The son born by the flesh persecuted the son born by the Spirit.
The same thing happens now.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ὥσπερ τότε ὁ κατὰ σάρκα γεννηθεὶς ἐδίωκεν τὸν κατὰ Πνεῦμα οὕτως καὶ νῦν

passages.text: But what does the Scripture say? “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with the free woman’s son.”
passages.sermon:
The Scripture speaks clearly.
The Scripture gives a command.
The Scripture says, “Expel the slave woman and her son.”
The Scripture explains the reason.
The slave woman’s son will not share in the inheritance.
The free woman’s son will receive the inheritance.
The slave woman’s son will not inherit together with the free woman’s son.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ τί λέγει ἡ γραφή Ἔκβαλε τὴν παιδίσκην καὶ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτῆς οὐ γὰρ μὴ κληρονομήσει ὁ υἱὸς τῆς παιδίσκης μετὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἐλευθέρας

passages.text: Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers.
He calls them brothers.
He says, “We are not children of the slave woman.”
He says, “We are children of the free woman.”
passages.original: διό ἀδελφοί οὐκ ἐσμὲν παιδίσκης τέκνα ἀλλὰ τῆς ἐλευθέρας
